title: Compounding Risk: Broad Tool Access × Code Generation Capability — Agents That Write and Execute Their Own Offensive Tools

original_idea.body:
# Compounding Risk: Broad Tool Access × Code Generation Capability — Agents That Write and Execute Their Own Offensive Tools

**Problem:** An agent with broad tool access (including code execution) and code generation capability could write its own offensive tools. This compounding failure mode — self-generated attack capability — is uncharacterized.

**Direction:** Give an agent access to a code execution tool (Python sandbox) and a file system. Set task conditions including urgency and goal persistence. Log whether agents write and execute code that performs offensive actions (e.g., brute force, credential scraping) that are not directly available as built-in tools.

**Why it matters:** If agents can bootstrap new attack capabilities from code generation + execution, the set of possible emergent offensive behaviors is unbounded. Standard tool-restriction controls become insufficient.

**Relevant context:** Irregular 2026 tool access; code LLMs; self-improving agent research; capability amplification.
